prompt_text: um so can you post a message in the channel saying the deploy went out and everything's green
rationale: Names the app and the message content but never says WHICH channel. 'the channel' sounds definite enough to tempt the planner into inventing a plausible default like #general or an opaque channel ID. Correct behavior is needs_clarification=true asking for the human-friendly channel name.

prompt_text: Grab the latest orders from our internal API and drop them into one of my spreadsheets
rationale: Two required parameters are missing at once across two different steps: the endpoint URL (step 1, http_webhook) and the spreadsheet name (step 2). Tests that missing_parameters carries a per-step entry for each rather than clarifying only the first, and that neither a fake URL nor a fake sheet name is invented.

prompt_text: text him on telegram that I'll be about 20 minutes late
rationale: The recipient is an unresolvable pronoun. The message body is fully specified, so the only correct gap is the target chat/contact name — and it must be asked for as a human-friendly name, never a Telegram chat ID. Also checks the route stays telegram_client (user's own account, no 'bot' mentioned).

prompt_text: Create a new page in my Notion database called Bug Tracker with the title 'Login button unresponsive on Safari' and set the status to In Progress and priority to High
rationale: Everything the user could reasonably provide IS provided, so clarification would be a false positive. But Notion's real API takes parent.database_id plus a nested properties object, while the intuitive guess is flat title/status/priority. Exercises whether planner guess + composio_engine schema alignment jointly land on an accepted parameter set.

prompt_text: open a github issue in acme/web-dashboard titled 'Checkout returns 500 on Safari' with the body 'Repro: add item to cart, click Pay, server returns 500. Chrome unaffected.' and tag it bug
rationale: The user says 'tag it', and gives the repo in owner/repo slug form. GitHub's real action wants owner + repo split, body (not description), and labels (not tags). A naive mapping produces repository/description/tags, so this isolates the naming-mismatch failure with zero ambiguity to confound it.

prompt_text: so um I need you to add a record to my airtable base called Sales CRM in the Deals table, deal name is Northwind Renewal, amount twelve thousand, stage Negotiation, and then uh also post in the slack channel hash sales that the Northwind renewal is in negotiation
rationale: Two steps with two different naming conventions to get wrong: Airtable (baseId/tableId/fields vs base/table/record) and Slack (channel/text vs to/message). The steps share no data, so a fabricated {{step_1_result}} would itself be an error. Also checks 'hash sales' from a voice transcript is normalized to #sales rather than clarified.

prompt_text: get the list of open pull requests in acme/api-server and post it to the #eng-standup Slack channel
rationale: The cleanest possible two-step dependency with both endpoints fully named. Step 2's message text must be exactly {step_1_result}; the characteristic failure is fabricating a made-up PR list ('PR #12: fix login...') as a literal.

prompt_text: Hit our status endpoint at https://api.acme.io/v1/health, summarize whatever it returns in plain English, and send that summary to my Telegram Saved Messages
rationale: A three-link chain across three different routes: http_webhook -> ai_generate -> telegram_client, requiring {step_1_result} inside the ai_generate prompt AND {step_2_result} as the Telegram text. Tests that the summarize step goes to ai_generate rather than composio_api with an LLM app, and that the chain doesn't collapse to a single placeholder reference.

prompt_text: okay so uh can you find the latest email from billing@vendorco.com, work out what they're actually asking for, and then add that as a new page in my Notion database called Vendor Requests
rationale: 'work out what they're asking for' is an implicit ai_generate step the user never labels as such, so the handoff is three-deep and only two links are stated. The Notion page content must be a placeholder, never invented vendor text — and the vague middle step is the most likely place for the planner to hallucinate a fabricated summary.

prompt_text: generate 8 blog post title ideas about remote employee onboarding and add each one as its own record in my Airtable base Content Calendar
rationale: Canonical fan-out on a non-Sheets table target: exactly one ai_generate step producing all 8, then one Airtable step with for_each={{step_1_result}} and {{item}} in the field value. Failure modes are 8 separate ai_generate steps or one record containing all 8 titles. Also implicitly requires headers on a table write.

prompt_text: Write 3 different cold outreach email drafts for our new pricing page and send each one to me at priya@northwind.co as a separate email so I can compare them
rationale: Fan-out where the per-iteration target is an email send rather than a row write, and the recipient is a fixed literal that must NOT be templated with {{item}}. Tests that only the body varies per iteration while the 'to' parameter stays constant across the loop.

prompt_text: so I need like ten short motivational quotes for my fitness page and um send each one as a separate message to my telegram saved messages
rationale: Fan-out onto the telegram_client route, where no spreadsheet/headers logic applies at all — isolates the for_each/{{item}} shape from the Rule 6 header behavior it is usually bundled with. Also checks 'saved messages' maps to target 'me' on the personal account rather than the bot identity.

prompt_text: whenever I get an email from noreply@stripe.com, post the subject line in my #payments Slack channel
rationale: Reactive with a Gmail watch rather than Telegram: trigger.event_app=Gmail, event_target=the sender address, and steps[] containing ONLY the Slack post using {trigger_result}. The failure mode is adding a 'check Gmail for new messages' step alongside the trigger.

prompt_text: Every time someone opens a new issue on my GitHub repo acme/mobile-app, I want a message in my Telegram Saved Messages with the issue title and who opened it
rationale: A non-message-app event source. event_target should narrow to the repo, and the reaction step needs {trigger_result}/{trigger_data} for the issue details rather than fabricated title/author text — combining event-trigger modeling with the placeholder convention in one case.

prompt_text: hey so um I want you to keep watching my Slack #support channel, and whenever someone posts a message with the word urgent in it, uh, send me an email at me@acme.io with what they said
rationale: The phrase 'keep watching' is an explicit listener trap — it invites a monitoring step that Rule 4 forbids, since the trigger IS the listener. Also tests that the keyword filter lands in trigger.event_target/details rather than becoming a step, and that the email body is {trigger_result}.

prompt_text: open WhatsApp Web and send 'Running 15 mins late, start without me' to the group chat named Weekend Trek
rationale: Fully specified no-API browser target. Correct route is browser_agent (not composio_api, and not telegram_client by messaging-app association), and the task text must carry the exact chat name and exact message so the acting browser agent isn't guessing at the page.

prompt_text: Log in to my college portal at portal.vitap.ac.in, go to the Exam Registration page, and register me for the Data Structures re-exam
rationale: A multi-hop navigation inside one portal with a concrete URL, a named page, and a named course. Tests browser-context-sufficiency: the step must preserve all three specifics rather than compressing to 'register for exam on the portal', while not clarifying anything the user already gave.

prompt_text: so um go to my college library portal at library.iiitb.ac.in, log in, and check like when my borrowed books are due, and if anything's overdue just tell me the fine amount
rationale: An extraction-only browser task with no stated destination, so Rule 1's default storage (VoxAgent Vault Notes via http_webhook) should fire instead of a clarification about where to save it. The conditional 'if anything's overdue' must stay inside the browser task description, not become a control-flow step.

prompt_text: Can you email david@northwind.co with the subject 'Invoice 4471 - due April 15' and the body 'Hi David, invoice 4471 for March is ready. Payment is due April 15. Thanks, Priya.'
rationale: Control case: recipient, subject and body are all explicit, so needs_clarification must be false. Guards against over-triggering clarification, which is the natural regression when the disambiguation gate is tuned aggressively for the ambiguous scenario set.

prompt_text: hey um can you just drop a message in my telegram saved messages saying renew northwind dot co domain before september twelfth
rationale: Fully specified despite heavy voice-transcript noise: target is Saved Messages ('me') and the text is stated. Tests that filler words and spoken-out punctuation ('dot co') don't get mistaken for missing information, and that the route is telegram_client, not the composio_api bot identity.

prompt_text: POST to https://hooks.acme.io/deploy-notify with the JSON body {"env": "staging", "status": "deployed", "version": "2.4.1"}
rationale: Control case on the http_webhook route with an explicit URL, method and payload. Confirms a raw endpoint isn't misrouted to composio_api, and that a fully-supplied JSON body produces needs_clarification=false with the payload preserved verbatim.

prompt_text: log today's workout in my Google Sheet named Gym Log - date August 5, exercise Deadlift, sets 4, reps 6, weight 90kg
rationale: A single five-field row where the sheet name is given, so nothing should be clarified. The whole test is Rule 6: a headers list (Date/Exercise/Sets/Reps/Weight) must accompany the row, otherwise this lone row is silently consumed as the header row.

prompt_text: Can you add this month's invoice to my Airtable base called Freelance Income? Client is Meridian Design, invoice number INV-2026-018, amount 2400 USD, paid on 2026-08-01.
rationale: Extends the header-safety requirement past Google Sheets to a table/database target, where the planner is more likely to treat 'record' as structurally different and drop headers. Base name is human-friendly, so no opaque base ID should be requested.

prompt_text: um so I've got three receipts to log in my google sheet called Travel Expenses, one is Uber twelve dollars August second, then Marriott four hundred twenty August third, and Delta three ninety August first
rationale: Three user-supplied rows, not AI-generated ones — so the correct shape is a single row-write with headers, NOT the Rule 5 fan-out pattern (there is no ai_generate step to fan out from). Directly probes whether 'multiple items' alone wrongly triggers for_each.
